subtopic: Finding any percentage of an amount
title: Finding any percentage of an amount
subtitle: Percentages of Amounts · KS3 Maths
learning_objective: I can find any percentage of an amount using a calculator or written method.

key_vocab.definition: To find any percentage of an amount, write the percentage as a decimal or fraction and multiply. This method works for whole and decimal percentages.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can find any percentage of an amount using a calculator or written method.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Finding any percentage -- To find any percentage of an amount, write the percentage as a decimal or fraction and multiply. This method works for whole and decimal percentages.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Any percentage can be found by converting to a decimal and multiplying.
P% of n = &frac{P}{100} × n
Works for any P, including decimals and values over 100

Key examples:
  ✓ 23% of 400 = 0.23 × 400 = 92  (decimal multiplier)
  ✓ 7.5% of 80 = 0.075 × 80 = 6  (decimal percentage)
  ✓ 110% of 50 = 1.10 × 50 = 55  (more than 100%)
  ✗ 23% of 400 = 23 × 400  (must divide 23 by 100 first)
  ✗ 7.5% of 80 = 7.5 × 80 = 600  (forgot to convert to decimal)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – whole number percentage
  Find 37% of 250
  Convert: 37% = 0.37
  0.37 × 250
  = 92.5
  = 92.5
  (Divide the percentage by 100 to get the decimal multiplier.)

Example 2 – decimal percentage
  Find 3.5% of 600
  Convert: 3.5% = 0.035
  0.035 × 600
  = 21
  = 21
  (Decimal percentages work the same way.)

sections.title: Whole number percentages
sections.content:
Convert to a decimal and multiply.

(a) 23% of 300
(b) 47% of 200
(c) 68% of 50
(d) 89% of 400

sections.title: Decimal percentages
sections.content:
Find each percentage.

(a) 2.5% of 800
(b) 4.5% of 200
(c) 0.5% of 1000
(d) 12.5% of 64

sections.title: Percentages over 100
sections.content:
Calculate percentages greater than 100%.

(a) 150% of 60
(b) 200% of 45
(c) 175% of 80
(d) 110% of 250

sections.title: Real-world percentages
sections.content:
Solve each problem.

(a) A meal costs £65. Service charge is 12.5%. How much is the charge?
(b) A savings account has £3400. Interest rate is 1.5%. How much interest?
(c) 33% of 270 students walk to school. How many?
(d) A laptop was £800. It has lost 17.5% of value. Loss in pounds?

sections.title: Mixed percentage questions
sections.content:
Calculate each one.

(a) 78% of 150
(b) 0.1% of 5000
(c) 6.25% of 480
(d) 130% of 90
(e) 99% of 300

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✓ 37% of 250 = 0.37 × 250
✗ 7.5% = 0.75 as a decimal
✓ 125% of 80 is greater than 80
✗ 0.5% of 1000 = 50
✓ 3.5% = 0.035 as a decimal
